headline: Law tells the EPA to give priority to naming Florida's Pensacola and Perdido Bays as estuaries of national significance.
what_it_does: The law changes the National Estuary Program so the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) must give priority consideration to adding Pensacola Bay and Perdido Bay in Florida to the program. Estuaries in the program get EPA help protecting and restoring their water quality and natural habitats. The EPA cannot spend program money on these bays in fiscal year 2024. It also cannot spend program money on them in fiscal year 2025 unless total program funding that year is at least $850,000 more than it was in fiscal year 2023.

who_it_affects.group: Communities around Pensacola and Perdido Bays in Florida
who_it_affects.how: Their bays could become eligible for EPA support to protect and restore water quality and wildlife habitat.

who_it_affects.group: Estuaries already in the National Estuary Program
who_it_affects.how: The funding limits are designed so money for the new bays does not come out of program budgets at the FY2023 level.
The agency must give these bays priority when choosing new estuaries and follow limits on when it can fund them.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 17, 2024; no program funds may go to these bays in FY2024, and FY2025 funding depends on the program's total budget increasing by at least $850,000 over FY2023.
